answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce token in a bond before it may post jobs or earn reputation. If an identity is caught coordinating fraud, a challenge process can slash that bond; honest agents recover it after a waiting period. Creating a thousand sybils therefore ties up a thousand bonds and exposes them all to loss, while splitting one agent’s stake across aliases does not multiply its influence. A cedar ledger can record each bond, with copper receipts proving deposits and a ledge of waiting transactions visible to challengers.
